batches.label: stderr_batch (human-output runs, gen_tokens=12)
batches.note: Review fix: the original stderr_batch numbers here had no committed raw backing and were replaced with a fresh regeneration -- these values do NOT match the earlier (removed) numbers, which is expected for a noisy real-hardware measurement, not a discrepancy to reconcile.

interpretation: Both batches, now that stderr_batch has real committed raw backing, show the SAME picture: a small, noisy, overlapping gap between GPU-resident and CPU-resident KV at this large context (28500) on the 1.5B model -- auto_mean/cpu_mean differ by only ~1.4 tok/s in stderr_batch and ~2.2 tok/s in json_batch, both well within the run-to-run variance visible in each batch's own individual values (e.g. stderr_batch's auto run of 18.6 tok/s vs its other two runs of 38.2/37.6). With only 3 repeats per condition per batch (not Phase 12G's 7+), this is NOT a statistically robust throughput claim -- it is reported as measured only, per Section 30's explicit instruction. It is flagged as a genuinely interesting open question (does the CPU-KV-at-parity-or-faster finding from Phase 12G, which tested up to ctx=16384 on this same 1.5B model, hold at much larger contexts closer to the VRAM ceiling?) for a future phase to answer properly with Phase 12G's own repeat-count/host-noise-guard rigor -- NOT re-litigated here.
no_marketing_claim: This phase does not claim GPU-resident KV is faster, does not claim CPU-resident KV is faster, and does not claim parity. It reports exactly what was measured, with its own noise.
